trace.final_message:
I added `hourglass/gaps.py` with `gap_labels(worked, opening)`, and the commit is done. It returns one label per uncovered stretch, in time order, such as `gap 12:00-13:00 (60 min)`. It raises `ValueError` if any worked span falls outside opening hours. Overlapping worked spans are merged first, so they never produce a false gap.

I added `tests/test_gaps.py`. It covers a gap in the middle, gaps at both ends, overlapping spans, nobody working, and a span outside opening hours. The full suite passes under `make check`.

The new files follow the project conventions, including the owner comment, short functions and lines, and reverse-sorted imports. I did not run `git diff` before committing. I looked at the staged stat and the two new files only.

I did not export the function from `hourglass/__init__.py`, to keep the change minimal. That is a one-line addition if you want it.
